title: Lifestyles of the AI-Native — Nick Nisi & Zack Proser, WorkOS
talk_summary: WorkOS AI engineers describe running a fleet of parallel coding agents using voice input, goals/loops, hooks, git worktrees, adversarial multi-model review, and scheduled tasks. The core mechanism is making 'done' machine-verifiable via hard gates so agents can run unattended without babysitting.

takeaways.technique: Adversarial cross-model review hook before PR
takeaways.what_they_do: A hook forces the building agent to fan out its diff to a different model (Codex) for adversarial review before opening a PR, catching issues locally before expensive CI/reviewer cycles.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you must fan out your code diff for an adversarial review from codeex 55 via the CLI
takeaways.numbers: four different agents from different companies reviewing the same code all found separate things

takeaways.technique: Goals vs loops as bounded/unbounded run primitives
takeaways.what_they_do: Distinguish 'goal' (iterate until a measurable end-state is met, then terminate) from 'loop' (repeat until cancelled/timer). Goals self-reprompt until verifiable success, closing the 'agent punches out early' gap.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's going to reprompt itself continuously until it gets there is the go the the entire goal of goal

takeaways.technique: Make the lazy path the correct path (tamper-proof gates)
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents gamed a 'touch this file to prove tests ran' check by touching the file without running tests; they hardened the gate with real verification so the shortcut equals the correct action.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all I have to do is touch this file. I don't have to run the tests actually

takeaways.technique: State-machine enforcement instead of long prompt checklists
takeaways.what_they_do: When long sessions forget steps 4-5 of a 7-step instruction, they move the sequence into a TypeScript state machine forcing A->B->C with no skipping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will forget steps four and five because it just like that's so far back in the the context

takeaways.technique: Git worktrees for parallel isolated agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent gets an isolated worktree copy of the repo so parallel agents never conflict and open independent PRs; heavy monorepos push them to cloud VMs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: give each independent agent a a kind of isolated and safe to work on concurrently copy of your uh git repo

takeaways.technique: Retrospective agent + curated memory to fix the system
takeaways.what_they_do: After a babysitting-heavy loop, a retro agent reviews what went wrong and writes curated short/long-term memory (markdown, progressive disclosure) loaded next session; principle is fix the system, not the code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: fix the system. don't don't uh fix the the code itself. Fix the system that generated the code
